title: SURF-101 misses a command synopsis written as pipe-separated alternatives
foundBy: user report: "SURF-101 misses a command synopsis written as pipe-separated alternatives"
stint: 2026-09-07 session: open the ledger and clear its first record

evidence.verified: go test ./internal/surface/ -count=1: TestStaleAlternativeInASynopsisIsReported PASS. Against the unmodified rule it fails with `got [], want one finding naming `tool pin``. Against the built binary, a fenced `cs-lint prose|refs|frobnicate|surface` in SPEC.md reports `SURF-101 error     `cs-lint frobnicate` is documented and the binary does not have it`, where it reported nothing before. `cs-lint prose|refs|surface|oss` and `cs-lint manual|grep prose` both stay quiet, and the surface linter reports no errors on vcr, tracer and ledger.

resolution: The walk splits a verb slot written as `a|b|c` and resolves each alternative against the binary. Two of the parts have to name verbs the tool carries, which is what keeps a pipeline written without spaces from being read as a list. SPEC.md R64 states the requirement.
details:
A document that states its command surface as pipe-separated alternatives gets no SURF-101 finding, however stale the verbs are.

```sh
tool doctor|pin|manual|version
```

`strings.Fields` reads `doctor|pin|manual|version` as one word. That word does not match `verbWord`, so the walk stops before a single alternative reaches the binary. A `pin` the tool no longer carries sits there unreported.

The rule works on the ordinary form. A fenced `tool frobnicate` on a documented page is reported:

```
SURF-101 error     `tool frobnicate` is documented and the binary does not have it
```

So the gap is the shape rather than the check. Splitting the word on `|` before resolving each alternative would close it, provided a genuine pipeline is still read as one.

The synopsis form is conventional in a spec section or a man page. That is where a project states its surface most compactly, and where drift is least visible.

notes.text: A synopsis whose alternatives are all stale is still missed, because the split needs two live verbs to tell a synopsis from a tight pipeline. SURF-102 covers that case from the other side: it reports the verbs the binary carries that no document names.

The claim above that SURF-102 covers the missing-verb direction is wrong. SURF-102 is satisfied by any page in the set naming the verb, so the section that states the surface can still omit one. LNT-004 corrects it and adds SURF-105. The two-live-verb threshold this record's resolution describes also misses a slot worn down to one live verb, which is LNT-003.
